title: Preserve valid form input
summary: Retain user-entered values across validation failures, navigation within a transaction, and recoverable interruptions whenever doing so is safe.
problem: Erasing correct answers after one invalid field turns small mistakes into repeated work and increases abandonment.
use_when: A submission can fail validation or a multi-step transaction allows correction
Returning to a previous step is part of the intended flow
avoid_when: Retaining the value creates a security or privacy risk
The input is inherently one-time and must be invalidated
rationale: Users should correct the smallest possible part of a failed task.
Preservation also helps users understand what was accepted.

prefer_alternatives_if: Security policy requires sensitive fields to be cleared
use_if: A submission can fail validation or a multi-step transaction allows correction
Returning to a previous step is part of the intended flow

requirements: Return focus to a meaningful location after validation.
Ensure retained values remain associated with their labels and errors.
Retain valid answers after validation failure.
Prepopulate previously entered data when the user intentionally returns to edit it.
